facts.fact: The `linuxcnc` Post sets the class attribute `ROTATION_STRATEGIES = ("twp",)`. The base class default is `("dwo", "twp")`.
The `linuxcnc` Post sets `PLANE_COMMAND = PlaneCommand.G68_2` (from `Path.Post.TiltedWorkPlane`). This is the same value as the base class default.
The declare line of the `G68_2` plane command is `G68.2 X{x} Y{y} Z{z} I{a1} J{a2} K{a3}`. X, Y, Z are the origin of the Work Plane. I, J, K are intrinsic Z-X'-Z'' Euler angles.
The default align line is `G53.1` and the default cancel line is `G69`.

The Post writes the align line only when the Machine strategy is TWP, the Tool Axis of the Operation is tilted, and `twp_control_positions_rotaries` is true (default: true). When that property is false, the Post writes a `G0` rotary move before the declare line and writes no align line.

A non-empty `twp_align` value replaces the complete align line. The Post writes the text as it is given. An empty value gives `G53.1`. Test: `twp_align="G53.1 P1 Q1"` gives the line `G53.1 P1 Q1` and no bare `G53.1` line.

facts.fact: `G53.6` is not a default of the code. A reader gets `G53.6` only when the reader writes it into `twp_align` (label *Tilted work plane: align*, Machine scope, type string, default empty). The linuxcnc help text says: G53.1 moves only the rotary axes and lets the tool tip swing; `G53.1 P1` or `P2` selects one of the two poses; `Q1` lets the table take part; `G53.6` keeps the tool center point in position.

For one tilted Operation with `pre_rotary_move` set, the output sequence of the `linuxcnc` Post is: preamble line with the blend command, *Pre-Rotary Move* block, `G68.2 ...` declare line, `G53.1`, the moves of the Operation in plane coordinates, `G69`. The output has no `G0` line with an A word.

The Post writes the cancel line (`G69`) in three conditions when a plane is declared: before each tool change item and each Fixture item, before the declaration of a different pose, and at the end of each output section.

With two Fixtures in the Job (`G54`, `G55`) and one tilted Operation, the output has two declare lines and two `G69` lines. One `G69` is before `G55` and one declare line is after `G55`. The class docstring gives the reason: the control refuses a change of coordinate system while a plane is active.

The Post declares a plane only for an Operation whose Tool Axis is tilted (the local Z of the Placement is not world Z, tolerance 1e-6). A Work Plane parallel to the table gets no `G68.2`; the Post writes its Toolpath in world coordinates.

The export of the `linuxcnc` Post stops with a `CAMValueError` only when an Operation in the export has a tilted Tool Axis and the *Rotation Strategy* of the Machine is DWO. A Machine set to DWO with no tilted Operation posts without this error.

The error message for the DWO condition is: `{op} is on a tilted work plane, and this post-processor cannot emit the {strategy} strategy machine '{machine}' declares.` `{op}` is the Operation label, `{strategy}` is `DWO`, `{machine}` is the Machine name.
The reason for no DWO in the `linuxcnc` Post, as the class docstring gives it: `LinuxCNC has no dynamic work offset, so this post emits TWP only.`

The class docstring says that the tilted Work Plane syntax follows a LinuxCNC pull request that `is a draft at the time of writing`. The source gives no LinuxCNC release version that has `G68.2`, `G53.1` or `G53.6`.

The Machine Editor combo *Rotation Strategy* has these entries: `Not declared`, `Dynamic work offset (DWO)`, `Tilted work plane (TWP)`, `Post transform (not available yet)`. The stored enumeration values are `dwo` and `twp` for the two usable entries.
The `linuxcnc` Post adds the property `twp_kinematics_select`: label `Tilted work plane: kinematics select`, scope Machine (`SCOPE_MACHINE`), type `string`, default empty.

Help text of `twp_kinematics_select`: `A line emitted after the preamble when the job has an operation on a tilted work plane. G53.1 needs a kinematics type whose frames describe the machine; on a switchable module that starts in identity kinematics this is where G12.1 P1 goes.`

The Post adds the `twp_kinematics_select` text as a new line after the preamble only when two conditions are true: the value is not empty after `strip()`, and one Operation in `Job.Operations.Group` has a tilted Tool Axis (the Placement of its base Operation). The test reads all Operations of the Job, not only the Operations in the export.

The kinematics select line follows the preamble line that ends with the blend command, and it is before the first declare line. Test: with `twp_kinematics_select="G12.1 P1"` the line after `G17 G54 G40 G49 G80 G90 G64` is `G12.1 P1`. A Job with no tilted Operation has no `G12.1 P1` line.

The `linuxcnc` Post adds three properties to the common properties: *Path Blending Mode* (`blend_mode`, Job scope, choices `EXACT_PATH`, `EXACT_STOP`, `BLEND`, default `BLEND`), *Blend Tolerance* (`blend_tolerance`, Job scope, float, default 0.0, minimum 0.0, maximum 10.0, 4 decimals), and *Tilted work plane: kinematics select* (`twp_kinematics_select`, Machine scope, default empty).

The `linuxcnc` defaults of the common properties are: `file_extension` = `ngc`; `supports_tool_radius_compensation` = true; `preamble` = `G17 G54 G40 G49 G80 G90`; `postamble` = `M05`, `G17 G54 G90 G80 G40`, `M2` on three lines; `safetyblock` = `G40 G49 G80`.

`Constants.GCODE_PLANE` is `["G17", "G18", "G19"]` (`GCODE_PLANE_XY`, `GCODE_PLANE_XZ`, `GCODE_PLANE_YZ`). `Constants.GCODE_SUPPORTED` contains `GCODE_PLANE`, so the default of *Supported G-code Commands* contains G17, G18 and G19.

`convert_command_to_gcode()` sends G17, G18 and G19 to `_convert_modal_command()`. The base method writes the command name as one line. A Post can replace `_convert_modal_command()` to change this output.

`Constants.ARC_CENTER_WORD_NORMAL_TO_PLANE` is `{"G17": "K", "G18": "J", "G19": "I"}`. For a `G2`, `G02`, `G3` or `G03` command, the base conversion always drops the center word of the active plane from this table and drops no other center word because of the plane.
The conversion reads the active plane from `self.machine_state.Plane`. When `machine_state` is `None`, the conversion uses `G17`.

The active plane starts as `G17` in each output section. It changes when a G17, G18 or G19 command is in the Toolpath, and when a text block that the Post writes without change (for example the preamble, or a command with the `as-is` annotation) contains a G17, G18 or G19 word. The last plane word in the text is the active plane.

A Post writes a center word only when the word is in its parameter order. The common default of `parameter_order` is `XYZABCUVWFSIJKTQRPDHL` (`Constants.PARAMETER_ORDER`), which has K. These Posts set their own `PARAMETER_ORDER` list without K: `grbl`, `mach3_mach4`, `centroid`, `smoothie`, `generic_sheet_cutting`, `masso_g3`. A G18 or G19 arc of those Posts thus has no K word unless the order is changed.

facts.fact: Examples from the tests. `linuxcnc`, plane G17: `G2 X10 Y0 Z-1 I5 J0 K0` gives a line with `I5.000` and `J0.000` and no K word. `linuxcnc`, plane G18: `G2 X0 Y0 Z-10 I0 J0 K-5` gives a line with `I0.000` and `K-5.000` and no J word.

The code comment gives the reason for the rule: an arc gives its center in its plane; the center word along the plane normal has no function (a helix gives its pitch in the axis word), and LinuxCNC and Fanuc refuse it.

The Post compares a command name with *Ignore G-code Commands* (`ignored_commands`) and *Supported G-code Commands* (`supported_commands`) as a full name. Each line of the text property is one name, with space characters at the two ends removed. A name is not matched as a part of a different name: `G1` does not match a `G17` entry, and `G5` does not match a `G54` entry.

A command name that is not in the supported list stops the export with `CAMValueError` and the message `Unsupported command: {name}`. These are exceptions: a name in the ignored list, a comment, a bare T word, and a command with the `allow_unsupported` annotation.
A command name in the ignored list gives no output line, and the name is not necessary in the supported list.
`MachineState` has the attribute `Plane`. Its values are `"G17"`, `"G18"` and `"G19"`. The default is `"G17"`.
`Plane` is not in `MachineState.Tracked`. Thus `getState()` does not return it, `machine_state.previous` does not contain it, and `ms["Plane"]` raises `KeyError`. Read it as `ms.Plane`.
`addCommand()` sets `Plane` to the command name when the name is in `Constants.GCODE_PLANE`, and returns `False` for that command.

`addGcodeText(text)` reads only the plane words from a block of G-code text. It sets `Plane` to the last G17, G18 or G19 word in the text and reads no other word. The pattern is `\bG0?(1[789])\b`, thus `G017` also matches. A text with no plane word, an empty text or `None` does not change `Plane`. The method returns no value.
`setState(None)` and `updateState(None)` set only the `Tracked` values to `None`. They do not change `Plane`. A tool change does not change `Plane`.

After a `str` postable and after a command with the `as-is` annotation, the conversion calls `machine_state.setState(None)` and then `machine_state.addGcodeText()` with that text. The other state values become `None`; `Plane` stays, or takes the last plane word of the text.

`linuxcnc_post.py` is an example of a Post that narrows `ROTATION_STRATEGIES` to one strategy, sets `PLANE_COMMAND`, adds a Machine-scope `string` property, and adds a conditional line to the preamble in `_expand_prefix()`.
The `fanuc` Post does not change `parameter_order`. Its default is the common value `XYZABCUVWFSIJKTQRPDHL`, which has K.
facts.source: scripts/fanuc_post.py:100-135 (get_common_property_schema has no parameter_order branch); Constants.py:243

facts.fact: `EXTRA_SUPPORTED` of the `fanuc` Post is `G54.1`, `M2`, `M02` and `M30`. The Post adds these names to the common default of `supported_commands`. G17 is in the common list, not in the added names.

Example from the `fanuc` test: after `G18`, `G2 X10 Z-10 I5 J0 K-5 F10` gives `G2 X10.000 Z-10.000 F600.000 I5.000 K-5.000`. After `G17`, `G2 X0 Y0 I-5 J0 K0 F10` gives `G2 X0.000 Y0.000 F600.000 I-5.000 J0.000`. The `G18` and `G17` lines are in the output.

The `fanuc` Post has `ROTATION_STRATEGIES = ("dwo", "twp")` and `PLANE_COMMAND = PlaneCommand.G68_2`. `fanuc` and `linuxcnc` are the only included Posts that set these attributes; each other machine-based Post has the base class values.
The `opensbp` Post has G17 in `GCodeSuppressed` (`G54 G17`), which is the default of *Ignore G-code Commands*. The Post accepts a G17 command and writes no line for it.

The `opensbp` Post has G18 and G19 in `GCodeUnsupported`, with the comment `arcs are XY only`. The two names are not in its default of *Supported G-code Commands*, so a G18 or G19 command stops the export with `Unsupported command: G18` or `Unsupported command: G19`.

brief.notes:
Read these points before you write.

1. Goal 3 needs a condition. The base conversion drops only the center word along the plane normal, but a Post writes K only when K is in its parameter order (F28). Six Posts (`grbl`, `mach3_mach4`, `centroid`, `smoothie`, `generic_sheet_cutting`, `masso_g3`) set an order without K. Thus "a G18 or G19 arc keeps its K word" is true for the common default order, `linuxcnc` and `fanuc`, not for each Post. The customization page must state this condition.

2. `G53.6` is not a second default. The default align line is always `G53.1`. `G53.6` occurs only when the reader writes it into *Tilted work plane: align* (F6, F7).

3. The DWO error occurs only when an Operation in the export has a tilted Tool Axis (F12). Do not write that a Machine set to DWO always stops the export.

4. The kinematics select test reads all Operations of the Job, inactive Operations included (F19). The DWO check reads only the Operations in the export. These are different conditions.

5. `Plane` is not in `Tracked` (F35). `reference/scripting.adoc` line 541 says today that `getState()` returns the plane and the units; this is not correct for the plane. `output/mbpp-postprocessor.adoc` says the state becomes unknown "with each value `None`" after a tool change, a `str` postable and an `as-is` command; `Plane` is the exception (F38, F39).

6. Present text that this unit makes incorrect: `output/posts/fanuc.adoc` line 121 (`G17` in the added commands), line 127 (`XYZABCUVWFSIJTQRPDHL`, "without the K word") and line 197 ("has no K word"). `reference/scripting.adoc` already has a `G17, G18, G19` row in the command table (line 76); correct it, do not add a second row.

7. `output/posts/linuxcnc.adoc` does not exist. The directory `output/posts/` has `fanuc.adoc`, `heidenhain.adoc` and `genealogy.adoc`; use `fanuc.adoc` as the model for the structure. F21 and F22 are there for the property table and the defaults table; the plan says the page has only the specific features and links to the common pages for the rest.

8. The tilted Work Plane tests for the `linuxcnc` Post are in `CAMTests/TestPathTiltedWorkPlane.py` (class `TestLinuxCNCTiltedWorkPlane`), not in `TestLinuxCNCPost.py`.

9. STE conflict: interface strings such as `Tilted work plane: kinematics select` and the quoted error message are not STE. They are quoted as the source spells them, which the global rule permits.
